lines.text: Physical experiments are expensive. A NASA education slide estimates wind tunnel time at about $1,000 to $2,000 per hour. That is the facility rate only, without model build or staff.
A hardware respin is $30k to $80k by one vendor blog, so treat it as a vendor claim. For rocket hot fire we found no primary source, so we show no number.

The point is to screen bad ideas before anyone builds them. MuJoCo is the judge. Three.js is only the actor replaying a stored trajectory. Every number comes from simulation tools, never from a language model.
Demo one. This is a recorded, seeded, reproducible run, not live compute. We pick the roadster that flips on rocket thrusters.
The agent called 11 tools in order. This log is recorded.
At 1000 newtons per nozzle, the search did not find a solution in 149883 evaluations. That is weak evidence, not proof of impossibility.
At a lower 300 newtons, the flip needs 3.2 seconds but only 2.54 seconds are available. A necessary condition is violated: strong impossibility under the assumptions.
The optimizer's fix raises thrust from 1000 to 3000 newtons. Applying the fix.

A solution is found, but it works in only 3.6 percent of 500 sampled assumption sets, with a 95 percent interval of 2.3 to 5.6. It is fragile, and the model is simplified and needs precise validation.
Now autoresearch. The data here is synthetic and sim-to-real is not validated. We say this up front.

For attitude control, the baseline open-loop schedule succeeds in 5.5 percent of 200 disturbed samples. With feedback it is 100 percent. It is a toy 10 kilogram article, not a claim about a real vehicle.

The calibration experiment recommendation raises identifiable parameters from 5 to 9 of 9. In the verdict, the schedule controller moves from 1 to 66.5 percent. This is a self-consistent test where the model class matches the generator.

Verdicts are asymmetric. Found is strong evidence within the assumptions. A violated necessary condition is a strong impossibility. Not found within budget is weak evidence only, and we never call it proof.
Drift builds the sim. We kill ideas not worth simulating.
Luminary speeds up experts' simulations. We give everyone their first physical experiment.
The business model is a hypothesis and is unvalidated. We have not confirmed willingness to pay, and we have no customers or revenue yet.
Next: validate calibration against real data, add more templates, and run user interviews.
What we need: first users to test this hypothesis, and partners with real test data. Thank you.
